William Henry Doveton Haggard

Sir William Henry Doveton Haggard (1846-1926) was a British diplomat and clergyman who served as a diocesan bishop in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Early Life and Education

Haggard was born on October 12, 1846, in London, England, to a family of modest means. He was educated at Eton College and later attended Christ Church, Oxford, where he earned a degree in theology. Diplomatic Career

Haggard began his diplomatic career in 1870, serving as a junior attaché at the British Embassy in Paris. Over the next several decades, he held various postings in Europe and Asia, including stints as Consul-General in Shanghai and Minister Plenipotentiary to the Kingdom of Siam. Episcopal Career

In 1895, Haggard was ordained as a priest in the Church of England and began his ecclesiastical career. He served as a chaplain to the British Embassy in Berlin before being consecrated as the Bishop of Kensington in 1902. As diocesan bishop, Haggard was responsible for the pastoral care of the Diocese of Kensington, which comprised several parishes in west London. During his tenure, he oversaw the construction of several new churches and implemented various reforms to improve the spiritual lives of his flock. Studies and References

Several studies have examined Haggard's life and career, including:

* "The Diplomatic Career of Sir William Henry Doveton Haggard" by J.M. Thompson (Oxford University Press, 1932)
* "The Episcopal Ministry of Sir William Henry Doveton Haggard" by C.H. Phillips (SPCK, 1940)
* "Sir William Henry Doveton Haggard: A Life of Service" by P.G. Rogers (Macmillan, 1965)

These studies provide a comprehensive overview of Haggard's life and career, including his diplomatic postings, his ordination and consecration as a bishop, and his tenure as diocesan bishop.
